overview: The City Council and Community Development Board held a joint public hearing to review the proposed Boston Avenue Neighborhood Corridor zoning project. The boards debated building heights and use regulations before continuing the hearing to June 11, 2026.

items.title: Presentation of Boston Avenue Corridor Zoning
items.summary: Consultants presented the proposed Boston Avenue Neighborhood Corridor zoning project, which introduces three sub-districts (BA1, BA2, and BA3) designed to transition from neighborhoods to higher-intensity mixed-use areas. The plan includes a menu of community benefit incentives that allow developers to increase building heights in exchange for affordable housing or historic preservation.

items.title: Geographical Context and Landmarks
items.summary: Planning staff identified landmarks for the proposed districts, noting that BA1 covers the area near Tufts University, BA3 includes the Whole Foods market, and BA2 covers South Boston Avenue near Ball Square. Staff recommended removing Walkling Court from the proposal as it is already being redeveloped under a separate planned development district.

items.title: Board Deliberation on Heights and Uses
items.summary: The Community Development Board chair presented a counter-proposal to reduce maximum heights in BA2 and BA3 to 70 and 85 feet, respectively, to protect neighborhood character. Members debated the inclusion of drive-through pharmacies, private student housing, and the impact of zero-setback requirements on properties with topographical challenges.

items.title: Public Comment
items.summary: Residents expressed opposition to the proposed maximum building heights and the potential for private student housing or fraternities to disrupt residential neighborhoods. Speakers also raised concerns regarding traffic congestion on Boston Avenue, sewer infrastructure capacity, and the lack of green space in the proposed 90% lot coverage allowance.

items.title: Direction to Staff and Continuation
items.summary: The Council President compiled a list of potential amendments for planning staff to draft, including revised height limits, a definition for purpose-built student housing, and the removal of certain residential properties from BA1. The public hearing was continued to June 11, 2026, at which time the boards will vote on the specific revisions.
